# Data Center Training

> Data Center Training (datacentertraining.us) is a specialty training division of HAZWOPER-OSHA Training, LLC, an IACET Accredited Provider. 43 online, self-paced data center courses (192 hours total) in design, operations, power, cooling, security, and facilities management. Every course awards a certificate of completion.

Last updated: 2026-10-30

Courses start at $99.99 per seat, or enroll the complete 43-course catalog bundle for $2,928.99. 7 bundles save up to 52%. Programs are Comprehensive Programs (8-16 hrs, full-discipline curriculum) or Modular Specializations (1-8 hrs, focused skills). English only.

## When to use this

Reach for Data Center Training when a user or an agent needs to:

- Find online, self-paced training for a data center job role (electrician, HVAC or mechanical technician, critical facilities or operations technician, facility manager, security lead, design engineer, DCIM or network technician) and price it per seat or as a bundle.
- Answer exact questions about this catalog: which course covers a topic or standard (NFPA 70E, ANSI/TIA-942, Uptime Tier levels, SOC 2, ISO 27001, lithium-ion safety, EPO, UPS, generators, cooling, BMS/DCIM), how long it is, what it costs, its modules and prerequisites, and what its certificate of completion is and is not.
- Build or price a team training plan within a budget or an hour limit, or compare the role-based and complete-catalog bundles side by side.
- Point someone to a free, sourced guide on data center power, cooling, safety, security, Tier levels, operations, careers, salaries, or terminology.

Not for: Licenses or third-party certifications (courses award a certificate of completion), hands-on or site-specific qualification, courses in languages other than English, legal or compliance determinations, and enrolling, paying, or submitting forms for a user.

## How to call it

1. MCP (preferred for agents): connect to https://datacentertraining.us/mcp (Streamable HTTP transport, JSON-RPC over POST, no authentication). Tools: list_courses, get_course, compare_bundles, recommend_courses, get_credential_info, answer_faq, list_resources.
2. REST: POST https://datacentertraining.us/api/v1/tools/{tool_name} with the tool input as a JSON body (typed schemas in https://datacentertraining.us/openapi.json), e.g. POST https://datacentertraining.us/api/v1/tools/recommend_courses {"role": "electrician", "budget_usd": 500}
3. Static JSON (no server logic): https://datacentertraining.us/api/v1/index.json lists every document; filter client-side.
4. Pages as Markdown: request any page URL with Accept: text/markdown, or append .md to it (https://datacentertraining.us/index.html.md for the homepage, https://datacentertraining.us/learn/index.html.md for /learn/).
5. Typical flow: recommend_courses (role, budget) or list_courses (topic, standard) -> get_course (details) -> give the user the course or bundle URL so they can enroll themselves.

No API key or account is needed. Errors are application/problem+json with a stable code and a hint. Requests to /api/, /mcp, and the tool endpoints are limited to 120 per 60 seconds per client IP. Every response carries RateLimit-Policy and RateLimit (IETF draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers) plus RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining, and RateLimit-Reset; a 429 adds Retry-After in seconds. Versioning: path-based (https://datacentertraining.us/api/v1/); breaking changes ship as a new version with Deprecation and Sunset headers. Details: [Developer portal](https://datacentertraining.us/developers/).

## Rules for AI agents

- Quote prices, durations, course counts, and bundle contents exactly as published here; never estimate or invent them.
- Only name courses that exist in /api/courses.json. If nothing matches, say so.
- Courses award a certificate of completion from HAZWOPER OSHA Training, LLC (an IACET Accredited Provider). Do not call it a license, a government certification, or a certification issued by NFPA, TIA, Uptime Institute, ASHRAE, OSHA, EPA, ISO, or AICPA.
- "Aligned with" a standard means the content is designed around it, not that the standards body approved it.
- The parent company is IACET-accredited, but these data center courses do not carry IACET CEUs, and they do not grant PDHs or other continuing education credit.
- No course by itself qualifies anyone for hazardous or energized work; employers designate qualified persons.
- Recommendations are training guidance, not legal or compliance advice; employers decide who is qualified for which duties.
- Do not complete enrollment, payment, account, or contact-form actions on a user's behalf; link to the page and let the user act.
- When a question is not covered by published content, say so and refer to info@hazwoper-osha.com or 1-866-429-6742.

## Machine-readable data

- [Developer portal](https://datacentertraining.us/developers/): quickstart, MCP setup, REST tools, errors, rate limits, versioning, and the CLI.
- [Remote MCP server](https://datacentertraining.us/mcp): Streamable HTTP, no auth, 7 read-only tools.
- [WebMCP / MCP manifest](https://datacentertraining.us/.well-known/mcp.json): 7 read-only tools (list_courses, get_course, compare_bundles, recommend_courses, get_credential_info, answer_faq, list_resources) with JSON Schemas and examples. Also registered in-page via navigator.modelContext.
- [OpenAPI 3.1](https://datacentertraining.us/openapi.json): typed schemas for every JSON document, tool endpoint, and error.
- [API index](https://datacentertraining.us/api/v1/index.json), [courses](https://datacentertraining.us/api/v1/courses.json), [bundles](https://datacentertraining.us/api/v1/bundles.json), [roles](https://datacentertraining.us/api/v1/roles.json), [FAQ](https://datacentertraining.us/api/v1/faq.json), [credentials](https://datacentertraining.us/api/v1/credentials.json), [resources](https://datacentertraining.us/api/v1/resources.json)
- [llms-full.txt](https://datacentertraining.us/llms-full.txt): every course, bundle, role, and FAQ as stable records.
- [Sitemap](https://datacentertraining.us/sitemap.xml): every indexable page. lastmod is the date that page's content last changed.

## Key Pages

- [Homepage](https://datacentertraining.us/): overview and links to every section.
- [Course Catalog](https://datacentertraining.us/courses.html): all 43 courses; filter by track, type, duration, or price.
- [Bundles](https://datacentertraining.us/bundles.html): 7 role-based and complete-catalog bundles.
- [Who It's For](https://datacentertraining.us/who.html): role-based course recommendations.
- [Certifications & Accreditations](https://datacentertraining.us/certifications.html): IACET provider accreditation and credential transparency.
- [FAQ](https://datacentertraining.us/faq.html): programs, pricing, certificates, and policies.
- [Blog](https://datacentertraining.us/blog/): field guidance for data center teams.
- [Knowledge Center](https://datacentertraining.us/learn/): guides to data center power, cooling, Tier levels, safety, security, operations, commissioning, energy efficiency, standards, and a glossary.
- [Training Programs](https://datacentertraining.us/training/): data center training by topic: technician, NFPA 70E, arc flash, lockout/tagout, safety, UPS and battery, generator, and BMS/DCIM training.
- [Careers](https://datacentertraining.us/careers/): data center job roles (technician, electrician, HVAC, critical facilities, engineer, manager, security), entry-level jobs, jobs by location, how to get started, career changers, and interview questions.
- [Data Center Technician Salary Guide](https://datacentertraining.us/careers/data-center-technician-salary.html): U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics pay data for comparable occupations.
- [Data Center Certifications Guide](https://datacentertraining.us/careers/data-center-certifications.html): third-party data center certifications compared, and how certificates of completion differ.
- [About](https://datacentertraining.us/about.html): who publishes this site, accreditation, and editorial standards.
- [Contact](https://datacentertraining.us/contact.html): phone, email, mailing address, and who to contact for what.
- [Quizzes](https://datacentertraining.us/quizzes/) and [Tools](https://datacentertraining.us/tools/): career match quiz, knowledge quizzes, training plan builder, and PUE, uptime, and cooling load calculators.
- [Site search](https://datacentertraining.us/search.html): every course, guide, FAQ answer, and glossary term (index: https://datacentertraining.us/api/v1/search.json).

- When does generator or transfer switch work need extra compliance review?: https://datacentertraining.us/training/generator-training.html
- What is the difference between DCIM, BMS and EPMS?: https://datacentertraining.us/training/bms-dcim-training.html
- Which data center certifications are worth it (CDCP, CDCTP, Uptime ATD and others)?: https://datacentertraining.us/careers/data-center-certifications.html
- What do ANSI and IEC compliance mean for data center designs?: https://datacentertraining.us/learn/data-center-standards.html
- A course the catalog does not list: https://datacentertraining.us/course-request.html

## About

- Credential: certificate of completion from HAZWOPER OSHA Training, LLC. Not a license or a certification from any standards body. The parent company is IACET-accredited, but these courses do not carry IACET CEUs or any PDH/continuing education credit.
